nodes.text: The festival is winding down. The rooftop is empty, the evening sky streaked with orange and violet.
You lean against the railing and stare out at the campus below. Students trickle out through the front gate, carrying prizes and leftovers.
It should feel like a victory. You performed. The crowd loved it. But all you can think about is Hanami's face when she said the word "chronic."
And Cassian's fist hitting the desk. And Tiffany's trembling hands. And Laura trying so hard not to fall apart.
You can't fix any of it. But maybe you can be there. One at a time.
You find Cassian where you expected to -- on the roof, after everyone else has gone. His guitar is in his lap, and he's playing something quiet.
The melody is simple. Gentle. Nothing like the sharp, driving riffs he usually plays. It sounds like a lullaby.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: You don't have to stand there pretending you're not watching.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Sorry. I didn't want to interrupt.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: It's fine. Sit down if you want.
You sit. For a while, neither of you says anything. The guitar fills the silence.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: This was her favorite song. My sister's. I used to play it for her in the hospital when she couldn't sleep.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: Music was the only thing that made her smile in there. The only thing that felt real.
His fingers pause on the strings. The last note fades into the night air.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: When Hanami said that today... it was like being back in that hospital room. Watching someone you care about slip away and knowing you can't stop it.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Your sister... she'd be proud of you, Cassian. The way you play, the way you care about this group. She'd be proud.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: ...Yeah. Maybe. She'd probably tell me to stop brooding so much.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: You're not alone in this. Not this time. We're all going through it together.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: Together, huh. Last time, I was alone. I had to watch it happen by myself.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: ...But I guess that's different now. I'll hold you to that.
He picks up the guitar again and starts playing. This time, it's something new. Something that doesn't sound like goodbye.
The hallway is empty. Most of the festival booths have been taken down. But from around the corner, you hear a voice.
Laura is standing alone in the hallway, humming quietly, her eyes closed. She's running through the performance again in her head.

nodes.speaker: Laura
nodes.text: Oh! I didn't see you there. I was just... practicing.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: After the festival? You're still going?

nodes.speaker: Laura
nodes.text: I know it sounds silly. But today, on that stage... I wasn't scared. For the first time, I wasn't scared.

nodes.speaker: Laura
nodes.text: I'm not going to let everyone down. Not when it matters. Not after what Hanami told us.
There's a steadiness in her eyes that wasn't there before. The nervous fidgeting is gone. In its place is something quiet and determined.

nodes.speaker: Laura
nodes.text: If Hanami can push through what she's dealing with, then I can push through my fears. It's the least I can do.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: You were great today, Laura. Really.

nodes.speaker: Laura
nodes.text: Thanks. That means a lot. Goodnight -- and take care of yourself too, okay?
The club room. The lights are off, but a faint glow from the hallway spills under the door.
You push the door open. Papers are scattered across the desks -- schedules, setlists, notes in Tiffany's precise handwriting. Some of them are crumpled.
Tiffany is sitting at the desk in the dark. Her head is in her hands. When she hears the door, she looks up -- and you see it. She's crying.
Not the controlled, dignified kind. Real tears, ugly and raw, streaking mascara down her cheeks.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: You shouldn't be here.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Neither should you. Not alone.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: I can't lose this club. It's all I have. Without it, I'm just... I'm nothing.
Her voice cracks. The president, the planner, the one who always holds everything together -- she's falling apart.

choices.text: What do you mean, it's all you have?

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Hey. You're not going to lose it. And even if things change, you still have us. You still have people who care.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: You say that now. Everyone says that. But people leave. They always leave.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Then I'll be the one who doesn't.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: What do you mean, it's all you have? Tiffany, talk to me.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: My parents don't care what I do as long as I'm "successful." My old friends drifted away when I got too intense about everything. This club... these people... it's the only place I've ever felt like I mattered.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: And now Hanami is sick, and Cassian is shutting down, and I can feel it all slipping through my fingers no matter how hard I try to hold on.
She wipes her eyes with the back of her hand. Slowly, the mask starts to rebuild itself. But you've seen underneath it now.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: ...Go home. It's late. We'll figure out the rest tomorrow.
You walk home alone. The festival is over. The music has stopped.
You fall asleep with Hanami's calm eyes in your mind. Her voice. Her hands on the keys. The way she said "Let's give them something beautiful."
The next morning. Something is wrong the moment you step through the school gate.
The hallway near the clubroom is cordoned off. Yellow tape across the door. A cluster of students stands at the far end, speaking in voices too low to carry.
Cassian is standing against the stairwell wall. Laura is beside him. Neither of them is moving.
Cassian's face is completely still. Laura is pressing both hands against her mouth.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: ...They found her. This morning. Behind the building.
He stops. His jaw is clenched so tight you can see it from where you're standing.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: In a trash bag. Someone left her in a trash bag.
The words don't mean anything. You hear them, and they don't mean anything. You hear them again and they still don't.
Hanami Nakamura is dead.

nodes.speaker: Laura
nodes.text: She said she wanted to see the cherry blossoms this year. She told me that. She was going to--
Laura's voice doesn't break. It just stops.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: Tiffany hasn't come in. She doesn't know yet.
The corridor feels very far away. Sound like it's coming through water. Someone is calling your name but it doesn't matter.
End of Act 3.
